doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: Keeping his publishing and the success of Expansions and Garden of Peace
summary: Naive about the industry, he kept his publishing since Thiele stayed out of the way; Expansions charted and Garden of Peace was later sampled.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Have you been able to keep ownership over the years of your own music?

Yeah, yeah, Monk, like I said I was really blessed because I didn’t know anything about the music industry. A good example like when I did the third album, “Expansions,” and the record came out, I mean the record took off real wide. People were calling RCA and all over the world they said we need — so we had a rush back and reprint all kinds of new records and ship them out. And then they called me up and they said, “Lonnie, you’ve got to get a manager right away, you’ve got to” — they said, “you’re on the charts.” Monk I was so naive I asked, I said what charts? You know the Billboard charts and everything. And like you said Bob Thiele stayed out of the way. So Bob Thiele, a lot of the record companies would, you know, would take your publishing, but Bob Thiele, like you said, he stayed out of the way and I ended up with my publishing. And then later on in life I wrote a song in the studio one day, I just said, you know, I just want to play something beautiful. And I wrote a song called “A Garden of Peace” and I mean I’m talking about years later all of a sudden all the young kids all over the world, they fell in love with it. Jay-Z sampled it, Mary J. Blige sampled it, they all sampled it and sampling the song, and I didn’t expect that. It blew me away ‘cause it’s just a beautiful song, I played the grand piano then I overdubbed the electric piano. And I mean they loved it.
